flow cytometry is a useful method for the immunophenotypication of normal and neoplastically transformed MCs in tissue sections and in bone marrow aspirates, and it has been successfully used in the diagnosis and follow-up studies of MC diseases.

flow cytometry can provide useful information on MC disease, especially for the differential diagnosis of mastocytosis and other myeloproliferative disorders, for the identification and enumeration of MCs in the bone marrow of patients with mastocytosis, for the follow-up of patients with mast cell disease, for the characterization of MC subsets in the bone marrow, and for the characterization of the MC microenvironment in mastocytosis.

the flow cytometric analysis of human MCs can be used to identify MCs, to distinguish MCs from other hematopoietic and non-hematopoic cells, and to characterize MCs in a variety of clinical conditions.
